task_instance: Create a minimal Expo/React Native app (package.json + app.json with iOS bundle identifier and Android package name) and run the skill's quick-start flow to configure and produce an EAS production build for at least one platform (npx eas-cli build:configure, then eas build -p ios --profile production), verifying a real build artifact/build ID as the skill's core deliverable.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire core deliverable (eas init, eas build:configure, eas build, eas submit, npx testflight) is gated behind an authenticated Expo/EAS account, and EAS builds run as a paid cloud service on Expo's remote build servers, not locally. Running `npx eas-cli build:configure` in the sample project immediately produced: 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Log in to EAS with email or username ... Input is required, but stdin is not readable.' `eas login` requires opening a browser OAuth flow against https://expo.dev, which also needs live network access -- confirmed unreachable: `curl https://exp.host` returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' through the sandbox's outbound proxy. Even if credentials were supplied, this session's rules forbid account-bound/paid services and forbid working around network restrictions, so the build/submit step cannot proceed at all. Nothing past local eas.json/app.json scaffolding is achievable offline.
